target_query: how to delete emails from one sender but keep recent emails

drafted_by.identity: Claude Opus 5.5 scheduled editorial draft job (Claude Code)

sources.supports: from: (example from:amy@example.com); older_than:/newer_than: with d, m, y (examples older_than:1y, newer_than:2d); after:/before: with dates such as 2004/04/16; in:anywhere includes Spam and Trash; is:starred under the is: row; the negative-operator caveat that conversations with excluded criteria may still appear because Gmail identifies matching messages first; the page is the Computer variant.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-19 by the drafting agent. All operators in the decision table appear on the page. The page does not define whether after:/before: are inclusive of the given day, how many days 'm' represents, or result sort order, so the draft states those boundaries as uncertain. Applying the matching-messages-first caveat to positive age searches (not only negative operators) is the draft's reasoning from that sentence, presented as such.

sources.supports: Computer steps: check boxes, Delete at the top; select-all notification link ('Select all N conversations'); recover from Trash within 30 days; permanent deletion after 30 days or when deleted forever sooner; inside an open conversation, More > 'Delete this message' (conversation view must be on).
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-19. Confirmed the notification wording, the 30-day recovery statement and the 'Delete this message' option. The page does not explicitly state that a list selection trashes every message in a conversation; the draft infers it from the existence of the separate per-message option and words it as 'treat a list selection as acting on the conversation you see'. Reviewer should confirm this phrasing.

sources.supports: Turning conversation view on or off on a computer (Settings > See all settings > Conversation View > Save Changes); with it off, each email shows up separately.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-19. Steps and 'each email shows up separately' confirmed. The page says nothing about how bulk Trash behaves with conversation view off; the draft explicitly says this was not tested.

serp_review.query: gmail delete emails from one sender but keep recent ones
serp_review.observation: A standard web search returned general sender-wide deletion guides (blocksender.io, fyxer.com, mailmeteor.com, xfanatical.com, proton.me). At most they mention combining from: with older_than: or before: in a single line. None offered a keep-preview search, a way to keep the latest N emails, a rolling-vs-fixed cutoff choice, or the mixed-conversation risk for this job.
serp_review.limitation: A single standard search, US results only; not a full Google SERP capture.

information_gain: A 'what you want to keep' decision table mapping five keep rules (last 30 days, last 3 months, this calendar year, roughly the latest N emails, recent plus starred) to paired delete and keep-preview searches with a specific caveat for each, including the manual count-to-date workaround for 'keep the last N' that Gmail has no operator for. Also a two-search verify step (rerun older_than and newer_than) and a mixed-conversation explanation specific to sender-plus-age cleanup. The hub covers this in one line (from:sender older_than:1y).
overlap_check: Hub delete-all-emails-from-one-sender-gmail owns sender-wide deletion and has one 'Keep recent or important correspondence' line; this draft links there for address-finding and full clearance. Pending gmail-search-exclude-recent-replies owns the thread/recent-reply question; this draft covers it in two paragraphs only as it applies here. Pending gmail-older-than-vs-before and gmail-search-operator-older-than own operator mechanics; this draft uses them without a general tutorial. gmail-delete-old-promotions-keep-recent is the category analogue, not the sender one.
limitations: Source and documentation review only; no live Gmail mailbox test was run and no screenshots were produced.
Boundary behaviour of before:/after: (inclusive or exclusive) and the length of an 'm' month are undocumented; the table warns of boundary differences rather than stating exact behaviour.
The claim that list selection acts on whole conversations is inferred from Google's separate 'Delete this message' option, not stated outright.
Effect of turning conversation view off on bulk Trash scope is untested and labelled as such.
The 'this year' row uses 2026/01/01 and 2025/12/31 and needs updating after the year changes.
Google's help pages cited are the computer variants; mobile app behaviour was not reviewed.
